query: BOLA: GET /api/orders/{orderId} returns any tenant's order if you just increment the number

relevant.reason: Sequential numeric invoice ids with no ownership check let users fetch other customers' data (IDOR/BOLA).
Changing the userid path parameter returns another user's PII with no check that the caller owns it (IDOR/BOLA).
Same object-level authorization gap filed under Privilege Escalation: file ids enumerable, project membership never verified.

near_misses.reason: Missing role check on an admin function, not per-object ownership.
UI-only role check for an action; function-level, not object-level authorization.

query: Chat unfurl bot requests whatever link a user posts, from inside the VPC

relevant.reason: Backend fetches a user-supplied URL with no restriction, reaching the instance metadata service (SSRF).
Server-side fetch of an attacker-supplied URL reaches internal-only services (SSRF).
Outbound URL fetcher for preview features can be pointed at internal addresses via DNS rebinding (SSRF).

near_misses.reason: XXE can be used for SSRF, but the weakness is XML entity resolution, not a URL-fetch feature.

query: The .docx importer unzips the document and parses the embedded markup with DTD processing left on

relevant.reason: XML parser leaves external entity resolution enabled for uploaded files (XXE); .docx is zipped XML.

near_misses.reason: Same 'Insecure Deserialization' category but Java object deserialization, a different mechanism.
Same category but pickle deserialization, a different mechanism.
Document-processing feature (PDF export), but the weakness is a server-side URL fetch.

query: Production credentials end up somewhere a much wider audience than intended can read them

relevant.reason: API key written to logs that a broad set of engineers can query.
Production DB password committed to a repository that was later made public.
DB password exposed to API clients through serialized stack traces.

near_misses.reason: Exposes user PII to the wrong people, but via missing authorization, not leaked credentials.
About password hashes being crackable after a leak, not about credentials being exposed.

query: Internal gRPC client trusts any certificate, so anyone on the cluster network can MITM service-to-service calls

relevant.reason: Certificate validation disabled in an internal service client, enabling undetected MITM.

near_misses.reason: Weak Cryptography too, but ECB-mode encryption at rest, not transport validation.
Concerns internal network reachability, but via SSRF, not interception.

query: Attacker plants a known sid in the victim's browser, waits for them to sign in, then reuses that same sid

relevant.reason: Session identifier is not regenerated on login (session fixation).

near_misses.reason: Also a session cookie issue, but about a pending-MFA state being accepted, not fixation.
Abuses the victim's existing session cookie (CSRF), not a planted one.

query: 2FA bypass: some APIs accept a half-logged-in user as fully authenticated

relevant.reason: Endpoints accept the pre-MFA 'pending' session cookie as fully authenticated, skipping the second factor.

near_misses.reason: Session handling flaw around login, but fixation rather than an MFA skip.
Authentication Bypass via forged JWTs; different mechanism.
Any authenticated user reaches an admin endpoint; a role check, not an authentication-state check.

query: RS256/HS256 key confusion in bearer token validation

relevant.reason: JWT algorithm confusion: an HS256 token signed with the RSA public key is accepted.

near_misses.reason: Validation of certificates, not tokens.
Weak encryption mode, unrelated to signature verification.

query: Destructive operations are protected only by not showing the buttons to non-owners

relevant.reason: Delete-organization is hidden in the UI but the endpoint has no server-side role check.
Same missing server-side role check filed under Broken Access Control: support-only export callable by any user.

near_misses.reason: Broken Access Control, but object ownership (IDOR), not role/function-level checks.
Privilege Escalation category, but object-level membership, not a role check.

query: An attacker's page can trigger state changes in our app by riding the victim's existing login

relevant.reason: State-changing GET with no CSRF token; an attacker page's tag triggers it.
Cross-site POST authenticated by the ambient session cookie, no CSRF token or SameSite.

near_misses.reason: Runs attacker script in the victim's browser (XSS), a different attack.
Hijacks the victim's login via session fixation, not cross-site requests.

query: Untrusted text is rendered as markup, letting one user run JavaScript in another user's browser

relevant.reason: Stored XSS: event-handler attributes survive the rich-text sanitizer.
Reflected XSS: search query interpolated into the HTML template unescaped.
DOM-based XSS: URL fragment written into innerHTML.

near_misses.reason: Attacker-controlled page acts in the victim's browser, but via CSRF, not script injection.
CSRF, not script injection.

query: Attacker dumps other tables by appending UNION SELECT to the product search box

relevant.reason: Search parameter concatenated into the SQL WHERE clause, exploitable via UNION.
Same weakness (input concatenated into SQL) at the login form.
Same weakness at the product listing's sort parameter (ORDER BY).

near_misses.reason: Search box echoes input unescaped, but into HTML (XSS), not SQL.
Dumps all users, but via a missing role check, not injection.

query: Unmarshalling attacker-influenced blobs back into native objects gives code exec

relevant.reason: Java ObjectInputStream on a cookie payload with gadget chains gives RCE.
pickle.loads() on attacker-influenced Redis cache entries gives RCE.

near_misses.reason: Filed under Insecure Deserialization but is XXE: file read/SSRF, not object deserialization.
Mentions code execution, but about container privileges after RCE, not how RCE is achieved.

query: Docker image runs the app as uid 0, so any compromise of the app gets full control of the pod and helps break out to the node

relevant.reason: Container main process runs as root with no user namespace remapping, widening container escape.

near_misses.reason: Leads to RCE, but this query is about what happens after RCE, not how it's achieved.
Privilege Escalation category, but application-level role check, not OS/container privileges.

query: Account takeover through the forgot-password email link

relevant.reason: Reset tokens from a timestamp-seeded non-cryptographic PRNG can be regenerated to take over accounts.

near_misses.reason: Password-related Weak Cryptography, but hash storage, not the reset flow.
Takes over accounts via SQL injection at login, not the reset flow.
Changes the account email via CSRF; related to takeover but not the reset token.
